chapter: Family, Margaret's story and Eutris's memories
title: Lending records to be taped
summary: The interviewers ask to borrow three of his records to put on tape; he praises one with Cookie Williams and Rex Stewart.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Can I take these records and record them?
Sure.
I'll bring them back.
These are my records.
Yeah, I know.
Now, what did you ask?
He wanted to know if he can take the records and record them, 'cause it takes too long to do it here.
Sure... When it comes to music, she ain't got nothing to do with it. That's music. She don't make no records. I make them.
Nobody's saying anything about the records. He just wants to know if he can take the records. I'm sure you don't mind.
I sure don't.... How many you got? It's the other one I want you to hear.
That's why I want to take 'em, so I can listen to them, put them on tape, and we're going to submit everything.
How many you got there, one?
No, three.
Oh, you got the other one? Emmy, you look in there, please, and get - let's see what you got? That's what you got?
I thought you said you had one.
No, three.
Well, I misunderstood you... No, I don't mind, I don't mind.
This one he has already. He's not taking that one - just those three.
You're welcome.
Just take them and then return them right back.

That (Challenge) - that's it. Boy, that is a record! Lawrence Cookie I mean, music. I love that record... Williams, Rex Stewart, and I don't know who he is. It isn't exciting, it's just beautiful, the arrangement.
